description: ForgeOps — an AI DevOps engineer. Scans a codebase, scores production readiness 0-100, generates missing DevOps files, validates them with real tools on the developer's machine, and applies them atomically after explicit approval. Three tiers: Next.js frontend, FastAPI modular monolith, and a single static Go agent that dials outward only and does not trust the backend.

layers.name: Governance & Trust
layers.description: The chokepoint every mutation must traverse, the append-only audit chain, policy, identity and authorization. Nothing changes a file without passing through here.

layers.name: API Surface
layers.description: HTTP routers, the app factory, middleware, the RFC 9457 problem contract and the MCP gateway ingress.

layers.name: AI & Generation
layers.description: Six-tier model routing, the circuit breaker, the fallback cascade, the tiered semantic cache, rate limiting, and the generation pipeline that will sit on top of them.

layers.name: Analysis
layers.description: Codebase indexing, the plan analyzer, blast-radius classification and readiness scoring. Deterministic by design.

layers.name: Data
layers.description: SQLModel tables, the nine linear Alembic migrations, pgvector HNSW indexes and the two-role privilege split.

layers.name: Agent Core
layers.description: The Go agent's composition root, configuration, redacting logger, trace context and outbound session transport.

layers.name: Agent Execution
layers.description: The agent's mutation path, IaC runner, git client, validators, scanner and MCP server. Everything that touches the developer's machine.

layers.name: Frontend
layers.description: The Next.js App Router shell, the RFC 9457-aware API client, the validated public env contract and UI state.

layers.name: Policy as Code
layers.description: Rego for the MCP gateway and Cerbos YAML for resource-scoped RBAC. Each engine loads only its own subtree.

layers.name: Test Integrity
layers.description: The regime built after 419 green tests shipped over a broken gateway: wiring fixtures, signature conformance, the test-double lint, skip detection and the mutation harness.

layers.name: Verification & Checks
layers.description: The check scripts that turn a design claim into a build failure. Almost every one asserts a non-zero examined count.

layers.name: Build & Supply Chain
layers.description: CI workflows, Compose topology, pinned toolchains, hash-pinned locks and the signing/SBOM/provenance chain.

layers.name: Documentation & Specs
layers.description: The four read-only reference documents, the phase specs, the progress record, the steering rules and docs/.

layers.name: Future-Phase Seams
layers.description: README-only structural markers for behaviour a later phase owns. Deliberately not importable packages.

rules.summary: Repository-level tooling or metadata.

The app factory and lifespan. Composes 24 collaborators onto app.state, registers the six middlewares in reverse execution order, installs the RFC 9457 handlers, includes four routers and defines the three health endpoints. This is the callable uvicorn runs, and the callable every wiring test builds.
The ARQ worker entry point. Imports task modules so the @register_task registry is populated, then hands the handler list to arq.

The RFC 9457 machinery. A 38-entry registry pairing each problem type with its fixed status, a sanitiser that suppresses a whole detail on any secret match, and a non-disclosing 403 that takes no arguments so every forbidden body is byte-identical.
Structured logging with secret redaction applied to messages, args and exception text — formatException is overridden in both formatters, because that was the likeliest leak path.
Settings: the whole configuration surface with extra='forbid', cross-field validators, and a production check that accumulates every missing secret into one error rather than failing on the first.
Async engine and session factory, transaction-scoped tenant context, and with_ef_search — which uses set_config rather than SET LOCAL because SET takes no bind parameters.
RFC 8785 JCS canonicalisation, shared with the Go agent so both runtimes sign byte-identical bytes. Rejects floats with a path in the error.
OIDC token verification with JWKS discovered from the provider's own metadata rather than guessed, asymmetric algorithms only, and an exact issuer allowlist.
Backend core primitive: middleware, trace context, tenancy, the task dispatcher seam or the SSE event contract.

Identity and authorization — the OIDC authorization-code + PKCE flow, session lifecycle, per-route deny-by-default dependencies, the explicit public-route set, identity-derived blast radius, and the Cerbos client.
The governance chokepoint's data model — change sets, change items, validations, approvals and rollback handles. The six-stage transit and the mint-only MutationAuthority are task group 7.
The append-only audit event model: a BIGSERIAL sequence, a per-tenant hash chain and no foreign keys, because an immutable log that cascades away is not immutable.
Policy, evaluation and bundle models, including which side evaluated a decision — the double-evaluation invariant needs both recorded.
Secret storage model with a check constraint enforcing exactly one of an Infisical path or an encrypted value, so the database is not a second copy of every secret.

The stateless MCP gateway: header-based routing that never parses the body, OIDC verification before routing, OPA tool filtering, a Redis TTL cache with no process-local expiry authority, and the Tasks state machine with Lua compare-and-set.
Six-tier model routing: endpoint descriptors and adapters, the per-endpoint circuit breaker, the fallback cascade, the tiered semantic cache, BYO-key resolution and a Redis/Lua token bucket.
Generation-run records carrying the three-iteration bound as data. The bounded loop, the blocking gate, the advisory rubric and the template library are task group 13.
The codebase index tables and the Plan Analyzer: deterministic destructive-action classification and blast-radius scoring, with an approval gate that fails closed on an unknown verdict.
Project, tag and settings models, including the embedding backend that becomes immutable once embeddings exist.
Structural marker for Phase 2 deployment automation. README only, deliberately not an importable package.
Structural marker for Phase 3 incident handling. README only.
Structural marker for Phase 3 observability. README only.
Structural marker for Phase 2 notifications. README only.
Structural marker for the WebSocket hub, which task group 8 implements. README only.
Backend package marker.

One of nine linear migrations. Each carries its own gated proof: pgvector and HNSW, the two NOLOGIN roles, index extensions, change sets, policies, secrets, the audit triggers that REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE from the app role, generation runs with the iteration bound as a CHECK, and project settings.
Alembic environment and configuration for the async engine.
The shipped model-tier map and MCP server registry. Debt D1 was that the tier YAML had no production caller; Q-27 now asserts the running app's tiers are derived from this file.
Tests of the checkers themselves, with good and bad fixtures. A lint whose own tests are missing is a lint nobody trusts.
The negative-control manifest: one row per property naming the mutation that must make it fail. Currently one row of thirty-one; task 19.2 completes it.
The fixture that makes wiring tests impossible to fake: builds the app through create_app() and may substitute a transport but never a collaborator.
The capability gate: skips locally, fails when FORGEOPS_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1, and raises on an unregistered capability key.
The @wires declaration collector. Wiring coverage is derived by AST walk, not hand-maintained, so a newly composed collaborator cannot arrive untested.
Binds every cross-component call site against the real class with inspect.signature().bind(). The Phase 0 defect in one assertion, and it runs in milliseconds.
Integration test over the real object graph: real Postgres, real Redis, real OPA or Cerbos containers, and transports substituted at the edge only.
A hypothesis property test mapping one-for-one to a numbered correctness property, each with a declared negative control.
Backend unit test or shared test helper.
Backend build definition: exact pins, hash-pinned locks and a multi-stage image that installs the runtime lock only, with --require-hashes.

The agent's composition root. app.New builds the whole graph by constructor injection with no init() and no package-level state, registers closers in construction order and walks them in reverse under a bounded shutdown deadline.
The typed configuration loader: every value parsed and validated up front, so a bad environment fails at start rather than mid-operation.

Two constructors, one of which is the only one allowed. NewRedacted scrubs string, bytes, error, stringer and reflected fields; an AST test asserts no package under internal/** reaches for the unfiltered New.
The outbound-only WSS transport and connection manager, with JSON-RPC framing and a 16 MiB read limit. The agent dials; nothing dials the agent.

Credential storage in the OS keychain with a reported 0600 fallback, and the durable outbound journal — which cannot represent an authorisation, because nothing that authorises a mutation is written to disk.
The identity seam with a paired-device provider: a P-256 key generated locally and never transmitted, and a certificate capped at 24 hours renewed over the live session.
W3C trace context propagation: preserve the trace id, mint a new span id, reject malformed headers, pass tracestate through untouched.

Atomic file application — temp file, fsync, rename, parent fsync, reverse-order rollback — plus the path blocklist split by intent, because reading a real .env and writing a placeholder template are opposite acts.

The OpenTofu runner: bounded execution, pipes it owns rather than borrows, an environment built from an allowlist with no os.Environ() call, process-group signalling, and no apply — the interface exposes only Validate and Plan.
The GitOps client behind a TokenSource seam: branch, commit, push, open a pull request and poll it. Force push is explicitly unreachable and the token never reaches a log field or .git/config.
The agent's own MCP server, exposing exactly three non-mutating tools. Making this a mutation surface would create a second write path.
The fsnotify watcher — a seam, not a stub. AST parsing over wazero-hosted Wasm grammars is task group 11.
A Docker daemon reachability probe, used by agent doctor.
A Kubernetes API reachability probe over client-go discovery.
Ed25519 signature verification for a downloaded update. The updater itself is a later phase.
Structural marker for the named-operation executor and the nested-internal mutation boundary, which task group 7 implements. README only.
Structural marker for the agent's in-process Rego evaluator — the second half of double policy evaluation. README only.
Structural marker for the in-process validators (compose, k8s, helm, trivy, yaml). README only.
Structural marker for devtools discovery. README only.
A 49-line composition root: signal.NotifyContext on interrupt and SIGTERM, deferred stop and Close, exit 1 on error. No business logic.
A separate module pinning the Go development tools by version so `go run` verifies them against a committed go.sum, keeping tool dependencies out of the shipped module's graph.
A real OpenTofu plan fixture, used by the plan analyzer tests instead of a synthetic document.
Reserved for future public packages. Structural marker only.
Agent build definition: module and dependency pins, lint configuration, and the GoReleaser configuration that produces six CGO_ENABLED=0 targets with -trimpath and a fixed mod_timestamp.

The RFC 9457-aware API client. Every non-2xx path raises exactly one ApiProblemError or a subclass, a malformed problem body still preserves the real HTTP status, and transport failures carry a synthesised problem so consumers never see a bare TypeError.

The validated public env contract, parsed at module load. Direct member access on process.env is the form Next.js can statically inline, which is what makes the browser URL a build-time value rather than a runtime one.
Frontend library code: JSON-pointer to form-field error mapping, query keys and small utilities.
The App Router shell: server components by default, an accessible layout with landmarks and a skip link, one real Home link, an error boundary and a 404. No feature routes yet.
shadcn primitives plus the header, sidebar, theme toggle and providers. Every interactive file carries 'use client' on line 1.
The single Zustand store, holding UI state only. A test asserts no server-derived data lives here.
Vitest suites, including policy encoded as tests: every dependency exact-pinned, no middleware.ts, and the P-14 error-normalisation property.
The Playwright shell specification. There is no e2e CI job yet — task 18.3 adds it, so this runs locally only.
A k6 health smoke script.
Structural marker for the eleven Phase 1 feature surfaces. README only.
Structural marker for data-fetching hooks. Empty by design.
Static assets.
Frontend build definition: exact pins, a committed lockfile, Tailwind and TypeScript configuration, and a standalone-output image that converts NEXT_PUBLIC_* build args to env before the build.

The MCP gateway's Rego: tools filtered by the caller's blast radius, with an unknown tool defaulting to the highest radius and an explicit default allow := false so a deny is a defined false rather than an undefined document.
Cerbos resource policies for role-scoped authorization. Adding these to the tree OPA loaded recursively is what made OPA refuse to start, which is why each engine now gets only its own subtree.
Cerbos server configuration for the sidecar.

The AST lint Ruff cannot express: FO-TD001 through FO-TD004 forbid reassigning a spec'd child, a spec without spec_set, a patch without autospec, and any Mock under tests/integration. A suppression without a reason is itself a violation.

Consumes a pytest report log or go test -json and fails on any skip in the mandatory selection — and also fails when that selection is empty, because a selector matching nothing would otherwise pass forever.

Runs each property under its declared mutation from a temp directory outside the repository, asserts the run fails, and reports VACUOUS if it passes. The review's one-off experiment promoted to a build step.
Derives the cross-component call-site inventory by AST walk, so the signature-conformance test never contains a hand-written list.

Enumerates create_app().routes and fails when a route is neither protected nor explicitly public. It has to descend into _IncludedRouter because FastAPI does not flatten include_router — which is why it also asserts a non-zero examined count.
Connects as the real application role and asserts it cannot UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE the audit log, does not own the table, and that all three immutability triggers are installed.
Every CI job the completion criteria cite must exist. Extracts bold-and-backticked tokens, fails on a citation with no job, and fails when the extracted set is empty.

Static Compose validation from one source of truth: every image digest-pinned, no service overriding its runtime user to root, every default service carrying a healthcheck, and each policy engine loading only its own subtree.
The init scripts that give the two database roles a login from the untracked .env. The migration creates them NOLOGIN with no password, because a migration is committed source.
A standalone stdlib-only module that checks every concrete type satisfying a project interface carries a compile-time assertion — and fails when the discovered interface set is empty.
Starts the digest-pinned Authentik and Cerbos containers for CI, compiling the policy set first so a policy mismatch fails loudly rather than as forty confusing test failures.
Tests of the shell helpers, including the .env idempotence contract.
Shared shell helper for lock regeneration.
A verification, bootstrap or supply-chain script. The pattern to look for: it asserts the thing rather than a document about the thing, and it fails when it examined nothing.

CI and release. Every action SHA-pinned, permissions least-privilege, ten jobs today of the fifteen the design names, and a release pipeline whose GoReleaser to Syft to Cosign to Rekor to SLSA chain is self-verified before any provenance step runs.
The binding design and task documents for a phase. design.md is the authority; tasks.md is the plan; every decision, property and completion criterion is numbered here.
Standing instructions every agent session in this workspace inherits: secret safety, file preservation and autonomy, and keeping this journal current.
The teaching document. Start here if you are new: chapter 5 explains the defect that shaped every later decision, and chapter 9 teaches you what to be suspicious of.
This knowledge graph, its authored semantic overlay and the script that assembles it.
Architecture, API, development and deployment documentation. docs/development.md is the project's build-rules home.
Read-only reference document: the product requirements, FR/NFR tables, the eight non-negotiable security invariants and the success metrics. Never edited.
Read-only reference document: the six-phase plan with per-phase deliverables, completion criteria and explicit exclusions. Where a deliverable list and a criterion disagree, the criterion governs.
Read-only reference document: a technology-by-technology audit against the July 2026 ecosystem, with six changes out of fifty-plus choices.
Read-only reference document: the research study. Its §0 corrections supersede its own later sections, which still carry the pre-correction figures.
The durable progress record: phase and leaf status, completion-criteria evidence, the chain of custody, recorded deviations and the decision log. Updated in the same commit as the work.
The merge-gating review that found 419 green tests over a gateway that could not serve a request. Untracked and append-only. The single most important input to this project's testing discipline.
Repository entry point and quick start.
The local topology: eight unprofiled services with every image digest-pinned, every published port bound to loopback, and optional services gated behind the vault and tools profiles.
The command surface. help is the default goal, every target is .PHONY, and all logic lives in scripts/ so the same commands work on every platform.
The committed, placeholder-only environment contract, loaded by every Compose service as a required env file. Never holds a real value.
Gitleaks, Ruff, gofmt, go vet, Prettier and the local checks. The gitleaks hook uses always_run so the four read-only documents are still scanned even though mutating hooks skip them.
Secret-scanning configuration with a deliberately narrow allowlist, itself asserted by a check script.
Lockfiles are linguist-generated but no longer -diff, because -diff marks a file binary and makes the highest-signal artifact in a dependency bump unreviewable.

tour.title: Start with the journal
tour.description: Read chapters 2 and 3 for what the product is and how it is shaped, then chapter 5. Everything else in this tour will make more sense afterwards.

tour.title: The review that set the standard
tour.description: 419 passing tests over an MCP gateway that returned HTTP 500 on every request. Read Pass 4 and Pass 8. This is why the repository is full of checks that assert a non-zero examined count.

tour.title: The authority, not the prose
tour.description: design.md is binding, tasks.md is the plan, PROGRESS.md is the record. When any document disagrees with these, these win. Section 0.4 of design.md is the test-integrity regime.

tour.title: The test-integrity regime, in code
tour.description: Five mechanisms: a fixture that builds the real app, a test that binds every call site, a lint that forbids the exact Phase 0 mistake, a check that a mandatory test cannot skip, and a harness that breaks each property on purpose.

tour.title: The backend composition root
tour.description: Read the lifespan top to bottom. Every collaborator is constructed here, non-destructively, and the comments explain which failures change readiness and which change liveness. Then read Settings to see the whole configuration surface.

tour.title: The error contract
tour.description: The problem registry pairs each type with a fixed status; the sanitiser suppresses a whole detail rather than masking part of it; the 403 takes no arguments so it cannot leak existence. Then see the same discipline applied to logs.

tour.title: The MCP gateway
tour.description: Verify, then route, then filter, then serve. Follow the order and notice that a denied call does zero upstream work. This is the composition the Phase 0 review found broken.

tour.title: Model routing
tour.description: Six tiers, a per-endpoint circuit breaker, a cascade that terminates in a deterministic template rather than an error, and a cache whose second layer doubles as an outage fallback.

tour.title: Identity and authorization
tour.description: Deny-by-default is attached per route, which makes it visible at the route definition and forgettable by a new router. The last file is the check that pays that cost.

tour.title: The data plane
tour.description: pgvector with HNSW, transaction-scoped ef_search, and an audit table made immutable three ways — sequence, hash chain, and revoked privileges plus triggers. The check script proves the last one at runtime.

tour.title: The agent's composition root
tour.description: Constructor injection with no init() anywhere, closers walked in reverse under a bounded deadline, and exactly one logger constructor — asserted by an AST test rather than a comment.

tour.title: Where the agent touches your disk
tour.description: Atomic writes with reverse-order rollback, a blocklist split by intent, and a subprocess environment built from an allowlist that never calls os.Environ(). Note that the IaC interface has no apply.

tour.title: Offline durability without an authorisation on disk
tour.description: The journal records intents, never authorisations, so a queued item cannot be applied without a fresh trip through the governance chokepoint. Read D-41 in the journal's chapter 8 alongside this.

tour.title: The frontend contract
tour.description: One error type or a subclass on every non-2xx path, the real HTTP status preserved even when the body is malformed, and a public env contract shaped so Next.js can inline it at build time.

tour.title: The build and the custody chain
tour.description: Read the CI comments: most of them explain a defect. Then the release workflow, where criterion 16's self-verification deliberately runs before any provenance step so evidence exists even if a later step fails.
